question: Can PJM serve projected data-centre load growth in Northern Virginia through 2030 without new dispatchable generation?

framing.restatement: Can PJM reliably supply projected Northern Virginia data-centre electricity demand through 2030 without adding new dispatchable generation?
scope_in: Demand growth and electricity service in Northern Virginia in each year through 2030, with PJM-wide resource adequacy and local transmission deliverability considered separately.
The forecast vintage, geographic boundaries, baseline date for what counts as new generation, and operational definition of dispatchable generation.
Existing generation, retirements, uprates, renewable additions, storage, imports, transmission upgrades, demand response, and enforceable data-centre load flexibility.
Applicable resource-adequacy and transmission-security requirements, including peak demand, energy availability, outages, and stressed weather conditions.
A primary scenario with no new dispatchable generation within PJM, explicitly identifying any reliance on new dispatchable generation outside PJM or behind the meter.
Sensitivity to load-forecast uncertainty, infrastructure completion dates, and whether service is firm or interruptible.
scope_out: Whether new dispatchable generation is economically optimal or environmentally preferable to alternatives.
Electricity affordability, except where it directly constrains the availability of resources assumed in the feasibility assessment.
Treating annual energy balance, announced projects, or interconnection requests alone as proof that reliable service is feasible.
presuppositions: Northern Virginia and its relevant PJM delivery areas can be defined.
Projected data-centre load growth can be expressed as geographically and temporally resolved electricity demand, rather than only announced facility capacity.
The meanings of new dispatchable generation and reliable service can be specified; different treatments of storage, imports, uprates, and backup generators may change the answer.
A baseline resource portfolio and plausible resource, retirement, and transmission trajectories through 2030 can be identified.
Service feasibility can be assessed conditionally on explicit assumptions about project completion, imports, and load flexibility.
framing.answerhood: A complete answer gives a conditional yes, no, or scenario-dependent verdict for reliable service in every year through 2030 under an explicit no-new-dispatchable-generation scenario. It identifies the load forecast and baseline used, distinguishes PJM-wide resource adequacy from Northern Virginia delivery constraints, quantifies any capacity, energy, or transmission shortfall or margin, and states the infrastructure, imports, storage, and load-flexibility assumptions required. It also identifies how the verdict changes under materially different load growth, retirement, project-timing, and dispatchability definitions.

claims.text: Using PJM's January 2025 load forecast, its Northern Virginia delivery-area allocation, and the generation fleet operating on 31 December 2024 as the baseline, PJM can provide firm service in every year from 2025 through 2030 without adding fuel-burning generation capacity within PJM, including fuel-burning uprates or behind-the-meter additions. This outcome requires scheduled transmission upgrades, retained existing generation, non-fuel-burning additions, storage, and firm imports, with no import capacity attributed to new external fuel-burning generation.
claims.rationale: Retaining existing resources and combining transmission, non-fuel-burning additions, storage, and imports is a possible route to meeting incremental demand.

claims.text: Using PJM's January 2025 load forecast, its Northern Virginia delivery-area allocation, and the generation fleet operating on 31 December 2024 as the baseline, at least one year from 2025 through 2030 fails applicable resource-adequacy or transmission-security requirements without additional fuel-burning capacity. The failure persists after crediting scheduled transmission upgrades, retained existing generation, non-fuel-burning additions, storage, and firm imports not supplied by new external fuel-burning generation.
claims.rationale: Resource availability or local delivery constraints could bind before the forecast demand is fully connected.

claims.text: Under the January 2025 forecast and a 31 December 2024 generation baseline, Northern Virginia's projected data-centre demand can be accommodated through 2030 without new fuel-burning capacity within PJM if part of that demand accepts enforceable interruption during constrained hours, even where providing the same demand with firm service would violate reliability requirements.
claims.rationale: Interruptible service changes the demand that must be supplied during reliability-critical conditions.

claims.text: Allowing versus prohibiting new fuel-burning generation within PJM does not change whether projected Northern Virginia data-centre demand can receive reliable service through 2030, holding load, transmission, retirements, imports, and other resources constant.
claims.rationale: The binding constraint could be unaffected by the availability of additional generation within PJM.

claims.text: A result described as service without new dispatchable generation depends on counting new dispatchable storage, new external fuel-burning supply, or new behind-the-meter generators as outside that prohibition; applying the prohibition to those resources changes the feasibility verdict.
claims.rationale: Different operational definitions can describe materially different resource portfolios with the same headline wording.

claims.text: PJM's January 2025 forecast projects a PJM-wide coincident summer peak in 2030 at least 15% above its projected 2025 coincident summer peak.
claims.rationale: The scale of forecast system growth determines the incremental adequacy requirement beyond Northern Virginia.

claims.text: PJM's January 2025 forecast projects a PJM-wide coincident summer peak in 2030 above its projected 2025 peak, but by less than 15%.
claims.rationale: A lower system-growth trajectory would imply a different incremental resource requirement.

claims.text: For data-centre load assigned to Northern Virginia delivery substations, utility planning forecasts through 2030 use annual load factors of at least 80% and count demand during PJM's coincident peak rather than treating all announced facility capacity as connected demand.
claims.rationale: Data-centre utilization and the conversion of facility announcements into connected load materially affect peak and energy forecasts.

claims.text: Northern Virginia data-centre electricity demand has no projected increase between 2025 and 2030 in the adopted utility planning forecast.
claims.rationale: Flat projected demand is the no-growth alternative to the question's central demand assumption.

claims.text: The headline Northern Virginia data-centre projection represents announced facility capacity rather than a dated, geographically allocated forecast of connected electricity demand, so it cannot be interpreted directly as the load PJM must serve in each year through 2030.
claims.rationale: Facility-development pipelines and utility load forecasts measure different quantities.

claims.text: With no additional fuel-burning capacity after 31 December 2024, the planned retirement schedule and accredited non-fuel-burning additions yield less PJM internal accredited capacity in 2030 than was available at the baseline.
claims.rationale: Retirements and accreditation can offset additions measured in nameplate megawatts.

claims.text: With no additional fuel-burning capacity after 31 December 2024, accredited non-fuel-burning additions and retained existing resources yield at least as much PJM internal accredited capacity in 2030 as was available at the baseline.
claims.rationale: Retention and non-fuel-burning additions could prevent a decline in accredited supply.

claims.text: At least one otherwise adequate no-new-fuel-burning PJM resource portfolio through 2030 requires firm imports whose availability depends on fuel-burning generation commissioned outside PJM after 31 December 2024.
claims.rationale: An internal generation prohibition can shift rather than eliminate reliance on new fuel-burning supply.

claims.text: No additional dependable supply, storage contribution, firm import capability, or enforceable demand reduction beyond the 31 December 2024 portfolio becomes available to PJM by 2030.
claims.rationale: The baseline-only portfolio is the alternative to obtaining incremental resources without new fuel-burning generation.

claims.text: Some resources counted as available by 2030 are only queued or announced projects without the construction, interconnection, fuel, transmission, or contractual arrangements needed to provide their claimed reliability contribution.
claims.rationale: A project pipeline is not the same quantity as an operational or contractually deliverable resource portfolio.
claims.review_note: Accept A3 and A4. A1 and A2 establish what the authors assume, but neither links a resource actually selected and credited by 2030 to a documented outstanding prerequisite. Signed interconnection agreements, construction-stage status, available-to-build ceilings, and competing restart dates do not alone establish the original existential readiness-deficiency claim. Both arguments are carried only for the narrowed modeling-disclosure finding; their stronger readiness inference is withdrawn. This component finding does not determine which resources will actually be available under Q3.

claims.text: Under Northern Virginia's forecast load through 2030, removing at least one planned transmission reinforcement from the network model produces a thermal, voltage, or stability violation under an applicable planning contingency, while including the reinforcement removes that violation.
claims.rationale: Scheduled reinforcements may be necessary for serving additional load securely.

claims.text: Even with all transmission reinforcements scheduled for completion by 2030 in service on time, Northern Virginia's forecast load produces at least one unresolved thermal, voltage, or stability violation under applicable planning contingencies.
claims.rationale: The scheduled upgrade portfolio may not eliminate every local delivery constraint.

claims.text: Delaying a Northern Virginia transmission reinforcement beyond its forecast load-need date requires deferring a data-centre connection or imposing an enforceable load limit to maintain transmission security.
claims.rationale: Service feasibility can depend on the ordering of load connections and transmission completion.

claims.text: The transmission network operating on 31 December 2024 can securely deliver all forecast Northern Virginia demand in every year through 2030 without reinforcement or connection restrictions.
claims.rationale: Existing delivery capability could be sufficient without incremental transmission infrastructure.

claims.text: Under PJM's January 2025 demand forecast, no additional fuel-burning capacity after 31 December 2024, planned retirements, and only resources and imports available by their modeled service dates, PJM meets its applicable annual resource-adequacy criterion in every year through 2030 and serves demand in chronological simulations that include storage energy limits and stressed weather.
claims.rationale: A diversified portfolio could provide sufficient accredited capacity and chronological energy availability without new fuel-burning capacity.

claims.text: Under the same forecast and resource assumptions, PJM breaches its applicable annual resource-adequacy criterion in at least one year through 2030 because available accredited resources fall below the requirement for forecast demand.
claims.rationale: Demand growth and retirements could create a system-wide capacity shortfall.

claims.text: Under the same forecast and resource assumptions, PJM has sufficient accredited capacity in every year through 2030 but fails the applicable adequacy criterion when chronological modeling represents prolonged low renewable output, storage depletion, correlated outages, and extreme weather.
claims.rationale: A capacity balance can differ from an adequacy assessment that represents energy duration and correlated availability.

claims.text: Holding the remainder of PJM demand and the resource portfolio fixed, adding the projected Northern Virginia data-centre growth does not increase the minimum additional dependable capacity, energy, or operational flexibility needed to satisfy PJM's reliability requirements through 2030.
claims.rationale: Existing headroom or non-coincident demand could make the incremental growth nonbinding for system adequacy.

claims.text: An apparent PJM-wide surplus through 2030 exists only in annual-energy or nameplate-capacity accounting; the same portfolio has a deficit when resources are represented by accredited capacity, chronological energy availability, and deliverable imports.
claims.rationale: An accounting surplus can be mistaken for the operational capability required for reliable service.

claims.text: Synapse's The Next Decade in PJM and the Pennsylvania resource-adequacy report use conditional assumptions about resource deployment through 2030: completion rules for planned or construction-stage resources and economic build permissions for eligible queue resources. The Pennsylvania report also assumes a summer 2027 Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart while acknowledging reports of a possible delay until 2031. These disclosures establish deployment conditionality and timing uncertainty, not that any resource actually credited by 2030 lacks a necessary development arrangement.
claims.rationale: revision of C15: Accept A3 and A4. A1 and A2 establish what the authors assume, but neither links a resource actually selected and credited by 2030 to a documented outstanding prerequisite. Signed interconnection agreements, construction-stage status, available-to-build ceilings, and competing restart dates do not alone establish the original existential readiness-deficiency claim. Both arguments are carried only for the narrowed modeling-disclosure finding; their stronger readiness inference is withdrawn. This component finding does not determine which resources will actually be available under Q3.

evidence.text: Synapse uses the PJM 2025 load forecast as the basis for both resource-deployment scenarios and models unit-level PJM-wide capacity expansion from 2025 through 2035. This passage supplies no annual coincident summer peak figures or endpoint growth calculation for the requested test.
evidence.quote: For both scenarios, we used the PJM 2025 load forecast report as the basis for the load forecast.

evidence.text: Resource availability by 2030 is conditional on modeled project advancement: both scenarios allow all currently under-construction large-scale resources and 90 percent of engineering-and-procurement resources to be built if economic, and assume completion of Dominion offshore wind and selected RRI resources on specified timelines.
evidence.quote: all large-scale resources that are currently in the “under construction” phase of PJM’s queue, and 90 percent of resources that are currently in the “engineering and procurement” phase, are built (if economic to do so) by 2030.
evidence.location: p. 10, Assumptions on available-to-build resources, Large-scale AET resources, By 2030

credentials.credibility_notes: Strong evidence of model assumptions, not verification that projects will meet their completion dates or provide dependable capacity.

evidence.text: The Advanced Policy scenario permits active large-scale AET projects to reach operation by 2030 at twice historical advancement rates, whereas Status Quo uses historical rates. The modeled availability of additions therefore depends on improved project execution rather than solely on existing construction commitments.
evidence.quote: based on an advancement rate that is double the historical resource advancement rates.
evidence.location: p. 10, Large-scale AET resources, By 2030, third bullet; footnote 33

credentials.credibility_notes: The authors directly state the scenario assumption; it is not evidence that doubling advancement rates is assured. Footnote 33 restricts eligible active resources to queue entries since 2019 with expected online dates by 2030.

evidence.text: The Advanced Policy scenario assumes sufficient distributed resources, including demand response, to reduce peak load by 17 percent by 2030. This is a system-level modeling assumption, not evidence of enforceable Northern Virginia data-centre interruption agreements.
evidence.quote: The Advanced Policy scenario assumes that by 2030, there are enough DERs, including demand response (DR) resources, to reduce peak load by 17 percent
evidence.location: p. 11, Demand response and DER-enabled load flexibility

credentials.credibility_notes: Credible as a statement of the authors' assumptions; this excerpt does not establish contractual enforceability, resource availability, or the share attributable to data centres.

provenance.unusable: The assumed PJM-wide peak reduction does not establish enforceable Northern Virginia data-centre interruption or adequacy under C3's no-new-fuel-burning scenario.

evidence.text: The Advanced Policy scenario assumes demand response and DER flexibility can reduce PJM peak load by 17 percent, approximately 31 GW, in 2030, including existing demand response; Status Quo retains approximately 8 GW. evidence.quote: The Advanced Policy scenario assumes that by 2030, there are enough DERs, including demand response (DR) resources, to reduce peak load by 17 percent
evidence.location: p. 12, Demand response and DER-enabled load flexibility; footnotes 36–37

evidence.text: Advanced Policy assumes additional energy efficiency beyond PJM's 2025 forecast baseline, reducing modeled 2030 system energy demand by 17 TWh and peak demand by 3 GW. Status Quo assumes no such incremental efficiency.
evidence.quote: systemwide energy load in 2030 is 17 TWh (1.5 percent) lower

credentials.credibility_notes: These are scenario-dependent modeled reductions, based on all PJM states adopting a New Jersey-aligned efficiency trajectory, rather than confirmed resources or the unmodified January 2025 forecast.

provenance.unusable: An assumed incremental efficiency trajectory does not establish dependable demand reduction becoming available, and therefore cannot substantiate or refute C14's actual-availability claim.

evidence.text: The Advanced Policy model selects dynamic line ratings and two reconductoring projects that together increase modeled interzonal transfer capacity by 3,345 MW. The excerpt does not identify these increases as Northern Virginia contingency-secure delivery capability.
evidence.quote: Overall, this means an intra-regional increase in transfer capacity of 3,345 MW.
evidence.location: p. 16, Advanced transmission technologies bullet; p. 13, technology assumptions

credentials.credibility_notes: The figures are model outputs using assumed transfer-capacity increases of 10 percent for dynamic line ratings and 34 percent for reconductoring, not reported contingency-study results or guaranteed completion dates.

provenance.unusable: The modeled 3,345 MW interzonal transfer increase is not Northern Virginia contingency-secure delivery capability and does not establish any of the claimed network-security outcomes.

evidence.text: Both modeled scenarios add 9 GW of new gas capacity cumulatively over 2025–2030. Consequently, neither scenario directly tests the claims' prohibition on new fuel-burning capacity after 31 December 2024.
evidence.location: p. 15, Table 4, New gas row, cumulative 2025–2030 columns

provenance.unusable: Both scenarios include 9 GW of post-baseline gas additions, so neither tests C1 or C2, and their shared additions do not establish C4's counterfactual invariance.

evidence.text: The reported resource portfolios meet hourly demand in a modeled typical year; this statement does not establish compliance with annual resource-adequacy criteria under extreme weather, correlated outages, or prolonged storage depletion.
evidence.quote: The resource mix in each scenario satisfies demand in all hours of the “typical” year that was modeled.
evidence.location: p. 14, Section 2.2, Capacity Expansion Resource Build Outputs

credentials.credibility_notes: The authors directly qualify the scope of this result. The passage neither reports a reliability metric nor demonstrates failure under stressed conditions.

provenance.unusable: Meeting hourly demand in a typical modeled year establishes neither stressed-weather adequacy nor the accredited-capacity deficit required by C24, and the modeled portfolios include prohibited gas additions.

evidence.text: Synapse tests resource adequacy for 2030 and 2035, not every intervening year, using 750 combinations of weather, load-forecast error, and forced outages; thermal-generator outage probabilities vary with temperature.
evidence.quote: In total, this results in 750 unique combinations of weather, load, and forced outage conditions.

credentials.credibility_notes: The methodology is described firsthand, but this excerpt does not provide reproducible model inputs. Its force for C20–C22 is weak because the scenarios are not established here as satisfying the specified no-new-fuel-burning assumptions, and testing 2030 alone cannot establish reliability in every year through 2030.

provenance.unusable: The description of 750 simulated combinations establishes methodological coverage but supplies no adequacy outcome for the specified no-new-fuel-burning portfolio or annual accredited-capacity margins.

evidence.text: In Synapse's Status Quo scenario, modeled 2030 loss-of-load expectation is 1.6 days per year, exceeding the stated PJM standard of 0.1 days per year by a factor of 16; expected maximum annual unserved load is 9.3 GW.
evidence.quote: In 2030, the Status Quo scenario has an expected LOLE of 1.6 days per year—that is, 16 times the maximum of 0.1 days per year under PJM’s reliability performance standard

credentials.credibility_notes: These are conditional simulation outputs, not observed outages. Their force for C21 is weak because this passage does not establish that the Status Quo portfolio matches the claim's forecast vintage, baseline, or prohibition on additional fuel-burning capacity. The result concerns PJM-wide adequacy, not Northern Virginia transmission security.

provenance.unusable: The Status Quo reliability failure occurs in a portfolio with post-2024 gas additions and does not establish that the specified counterfactual fails because accredited resources fall below its capacity requirement, as C21 requires.

evidence.text: In Synapse's Advanced Policy scenario, modeled 2030 loss-of-load expectation is 0.04 days per year, below the stated PJM standard of 0.1; expected maximum annual unserved load is 1.2 GW. This establishes a scenario-specific adequacy result, not compliance with the question's no-new-fuel-burning scenario.
evidence.quote: with LOLE of just 0.04 days in 2030, or one day in 25 years. This is 2.5 times better than the PJM standard of one day in 10 years.

credentials.credibility_notes: The reported result is firsthand but model-dependent. Its force for C20 is weak because this excerpt does not establish a portfolio with no new fuel-burning capacity, does not test every year through 2030, and does not demonstrate Northern Virginia deliverability. Neither this result nor the Status Quo result supplies the annual January 2025 peak forecasts needed to distinguish C6 from C7.

provenance.unusable: The Advanced Policy result includes prohibited gas additions and additional demand reductions, and a passing 2030 LOLE result cannot establish compliance in every year under C20's specified assumptions.

evidence.text: For 2030, the authors' Status Quo scenario produces winter unserved energy across most hours, while their Advanced Policy scenario substantially reduces but does not eliminate January unserved energy; these results alone do not establish whether either scenario satisfies the annual adequacy criterion.
evidence.quote: The Advanced Policy scenario results in no unserved energy in December, much smaller amounts of unserved energy in January compared with the Status Quo scenario, and virtually no unserved energy in February.

credentials.credibility_notes: These are reported simulation outputs, not observed outages. Their force for C20 and C21 is weak because this excerpt does not establish correspondence with the claims' forecast, baseline, resource restrictions, or annual reliability threshold. Nonzero expected unserved energy does not by itself demonstrate failure of a probabilistic adequacy standard.

provenance.unusable: Seasonal unserved-energy results from mismatched portfolios establish neither a breach of the annual LOLE criterion nor an accredited-capacity shortfall under the specified scenario.

evidence.text: In the authors' modeled July 5–7, 2030 extreme-heat episode, the Status Quo scenario has evening shortages on all three days, whereas the Advanced Policy scenario avoids unserved energy with additional solar, batteries, and demand response despite having less gas and coal capacity.
evidence.quote: The additional solar, battery, and demand response capacity in this scenario allow the system to meet load and avoid an outage entirely, even with less gas and coal capacity
evidence.location: p. 26, Section 3.3, discussion of the July 5–7, 2030 simulated episode

credentials.credibility_notes: The comparison is a selected three-day simulation, not proof of adequacy in every year through 2030. Its force for the specified claims is weak because less gas and coal capacity does not establish no post-2024 fuel-burning additions, and this excerpt does not establish the required forecast vintage, import assumptions, or Northern Virginia deliverability.

provenance.unusable: The selected three-day simulation includes new gas according to E17 and therefore cannot establish either firm-service feasibility or unavoidable failure under the claims' prohibition.

access.answer: Synapse is directly positioned to describe which project stages and advancement assumptions its own scenarios count toward 2030 availability. Its account of unbuilt projects with signed interconnection agreements is explicitly attributed to PJM's June 2025 factsheet, rather than presented as independent project verification.

report.answer: The report counts resources conditionally on future construction and advancement: it assumes completion of specified construction and procurement-stage resources and, in Advanced Policy, advancement of eligible active queue projects at twice historical rates. It explicitly says policy and regulatory action is needed to achieve modeled deployment. Together with the documented unbuilt projects, this supports C15's distinction between resources counted toward future availability and resources with completed arrangements sufficient to establish their reliability contribution. It does not establish that these projects will necessarily miss 2030.

arguments.note: This is a single line of support from Synapse's disclosure of conditional resource availability, supplemented by its traceable account of PJM's unbuilt-project inventory. It establishes a deployment contingency, not a quantified capacity deficit or the failure of every queued project.

access.answer: The report's authors directly know their model's completion rules, build constraints, and assumed nuclear restart date; these are disclosures of their own modeling choices rather than independent verification of project readiness.

report.answer: The authors assume service for resources classified as planned or under construction in 2026–2027, permit conditional construction of queue-stage resources during 2028–2030, and count a summer 2027 Three Mile Island restart while acknowledging reports of delay until 2031. This supports C15's distinction between resources counted toward availability and resources with demonstrated arrangements sufficient to establish their timely reliability contribution, not a prediction that every such project will fail.

arguments.note: One line of support from the Pennsylvania report's own modeling disclosures. The argument concerns conditional project availability, not the adequacy of its portfolios under the no-new-fuel-burning restriction or the magnitude of any capacity deficit.

The inference conflates conditional future deployment with an established project-readiness deficiency. E7 concerns projects already holding signed interconnection agreements; E11 explicitly includes projects under construction or in engineering and procurement; E12 specifies a scenario-dependent advancement rate. These categories do not themselves establish C15's stronger proposition that an actually credited resource is only queued or announced and lacks a necessary arrangement. Being unbuilt in June 2025 is compatible with having arrangements sufficient for service by 2030. To establish C15, link at least one resource actually credited in the modeled portfolio to an outstanding prerequisite. This does not require proving that the project will miss 2030. (conceded by proposer: The evidence establishes conditional deployment assumptions, not an actual readiness deficiency among resources credited by 2030. Answering this attack requires linking at least one resource selected in Synapse's modeled portfolio to a documented outstanding construction, interconnection, permitting, equipment, or contractual prerequisite; proof that it will miss 2030 is not required.)

A2 collapses three different propositions into C15: assumed completion of a mixed planned/under-construction cohort, permission to build projects if economic, and uncertainty over a named restart date. In particular, E178's available-to-build ceiling is not an output identifying resources actually selected and credited. E183's competing restart dates establish timing uncertainty, not that the restart lacks a necessary construction, interconnection, or contractual arrangement. Authoritative knowledge of these modeling assumptions establishes conditionality, but not the claimed existential readiness deficiency. A selected-project record matched to an actual outstanding prerequisite is needed. (conceded by proposer: The completion rules, available-to-build limits, and competing Three Mile Island restart dates do not establish that an actually credited resource lacks a necessary arrangement. Answering this attack requires a selected-resource record matched to a dated, outstanding prerequisite, rather than build eligibility or schedule uncertainty alone.)

conclusion.answer: The evidence gathered does not settle whether PJM can reliably serve Northern Virginia’s projected data-centre growth in every year through 2030 without new dispatchable generation: neither feasibility nor unavoidable failure is accepted (C1, C2). The assessed scenario uses PJM’s January 2025 forecast and the fleet operating on 31 December 2024, prohibits subsequent fuel-burning additions, uprates and behind-the-meter generators, permits non-fuel-burning additions and storage, and excludes imports attributable to new external fuel-burning generation. The evidence points toward reliability concerns rather than an assured yes, but the retrieved results do not establish this counterfactual’s annual adequacy or Northern Virginia’s local deliverability (C16–C22). A defensible capacity, energy or transmission shortfall for that scenario therefore remains unquantified.

judgements.text: Firm service through 2030 remains undecided because neither the feasibility claim nor its failure alternative has supporting argument establishing the specified forecast, restricted portfolio and annual reliability outcomes (C1, C2).
judgements.rests_on: Neither claim has an accepted load-bearing node; the decisive missing observation is a matched annual resource-adequacy and local transmission-security assessment.

judgements.text: The retrieved PJM-wide adequacy results cannot determine the no-new-fuel-burning verdict because Synapse’s scenarios include 9 GW of new gas during 2025–2030, while PJM’s reported study-portfolio margins are not disaggregated into the stipulated restricted portfolio (C20, C21; E17, E66).
judgements.rests_on: E17 establishes the scenario mismatch, and E66 does not isolate the required counterfactual; neither adequacy claim is accepted.

judgements.text: Northern Virginia’s delivery feasibility remains separate and undecided because the retrieved material does not establish annual contingency-secure margins with scheduled reinforcements or with those reinforcements delayed (C16–C19).
judgements.rests_on: The decisive evidence would be Northern Virginia network cases identifying thermal, voltage and stability results, reinforcement need dates and secure load limits.

judgements.text: Interruptible service and alternative definitions of dispatchability remain unproven routes to feasibility because modeled flexibility and resource classifications do not establish that enforceable local interruption, storage or excluded external supply changes the verdict (C3, C5, C13).
judgements.rests_on: Matched reliability sensitivities and enforceable customer and import commitments are needed to resolve these claims.

judgements.text: Conditional deployment rules and competing Three Mile Island restart dates do not establish that a resource actually credited by 2030 lacks a necessary development arrangement, while the revised modeling-disclosure finding itself remains undecided in the evaluated graph (C25).
judgements.rests_on: E11–E12 and E177–E183 disclose assumptions, but the surviving A3 and A4 undercuts require linking selected resources to dated outstanding prerequisites.

what_would_change_this: A matched assessment showing compliance in every year from 2025 through 2030 with both PJM resource-adequacy requirements and Northern Virginia transmission-security requirements under the stated prohibition would support a conditional yes (C1, C20).

A matched assessment showing a reliability breach in at least one year after crediting the specified retention, non-fuel-burning resources, storage, transmission upgrades and qualifying imports would support a conditional no (C2, C21, C22).

Verified January 2025 forecast tables and utility submissions providing annual coincident peaks, energy, hourly profiles, connected-demand screening and Northern Virginia delivery allocations would resolve the load baseline and growth alternatives (C6–C10).

A unit-level baseline-to-2030 ledger documenting retirements, retention commitments, commissioning dates, resource-specific accreditation, storage duration and firm-import provenance would resolve the available-resource alternatives (C11–C14).

Contingency studies showing secure delivery limits with, without and following delays to named Northern Virginia reinforcements would determine the delivery conditions and required connection restrictions (C16–C19).

Matched sensitivities varying load growth, retirements, project dates, enforceable interruption and the inclusion of storage, external generation and backup generators in the prohibition would establish how the verdict changes (C3–C5, C13, C20–C24).

Selected-resource records matched to dated outstanding development prerequisites would ground the project-readiness concern; competing schedule reports or build eligibility alone would not do so (C25).
unresolved: Q1–Q5 have no accepted answer: overall feasibility, geographically resolved demand, available resources, local transmission capability and annual system adequacy remain undecided.

The amount and operating conditions of enforceable Northern Virginia data-centre flexibility, including recovery demand and reliance on backup generation, remain unresolved (C3).

candidates.title: An overview of the uses of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
candidates.snippet: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are of concern because of their high persistence (or that of their degradation products) and their impacts on human and environmental health that are known or can be deduced from some well-studied PFAS. Currently, many different PFAS (on the order of several thousands) are used in a wide range of applications, and there is no comprehensive source of information on the many individual substances and their functions in different applications. Here we provide a broad overview of many use categories where PFAS have been employed and for which function; we also specify which PFAS have been used and discuss the magnitude of the uses. Despite being non-exhaustive, our study clearly demonstrates that PFAS are used in almost all industry branches and many consumer products. In total, more than 200 use categories and subcategories are identified for more than 1400 individual PFAS. In addition to well-known categories such as textile impregnation, fire-fighting foam, and electroplating, the identified use categories also include many categories not described in the scientific literature, including PFAS in ammunition, climbing ropes, guitar strings, artificial turf, and soil remediation. We further discuss several use categories that may be prioritised for finding PFAS-free alternatives. Besides the detailed description of use categories, the present study also provides a list of the identified PFAS per use category, including their exact masses for future analytical studies aiming to identify additional PFAS.

candidates.title: A fluid-to-solid jamming transition underlies vertebrate body axis elongation.
candidates.snippet: Just as in clay moulding or glass blowing, physically sculpting biological structures requires the constituent material to locally flow like a fluid while maintaining overall mechanical integrity like a solid. Disordered soft materials, such as foams, emulsions and colloidal suspensions, switch from fluid-like to solid-like behaviours at a jamming transition 1-4 . Similarly, cell collectives have been shown to display glassy dynamics in 2D and 3D 5,6  and jamming in cultured epithelial monolayers 7,8 , behaviours recently predicted theoretically 9-11  and proposed to influence asthma pathobiology 8  and tumour progression 12 . However, little is known about whether these seemingly universal behaviours occur in vivo 13  and, specifically, whether they play any functional part during embryonic morphogenesis. Here, by combining direct in vivo measurements of tissue mechanics with analysis of cellular dynamics, we show that during vertebrate body axis elongation, posterior tissues undergo a jamming transition from a fluid-like behaviour at the extending end, the mesodermal progenitor zone, to a solid-like behaviour in the presomitic mesoderm. We uncover an anteroposterior, N-cadherin-dependent gradient in yield stress that provides increasing mechanical integrity to the presomitic mesoderm, consistent with the tissue transiting from a wetter to a dryer foam-like architecture. Our results show that cell-scale stresses fluctuate rapidly (within about 1 min), enabling cell rearrangements and effectively 'melting' the tissue at the growing end. candidates.title: Ultraflexible organic photonic skin.
candidates.snippet: Thin-film electronics intimately laminated onto the skin imperceptibly equip the human body with electronic components for health-monitoring and information technologies. When electronic devices are worn, the mechanical flexibility and/or stretchability of thin-film devices helps to minimize the stress and discomfort associated with wear because of their conformability and softness. For industrial applications, it is important to fabricate wearable devices using processing methods that maximize throughput and minimize cost. We demonstrate ultraflexible and conformable three-color, highly efficient polymer light-emitting diodes (PLEDs) and organic photodetectors (OPDs) to realize optoelectronic skins (oe-skins) that introduce multiple electronic functionalities such as sensing and displays on the surface of human skin. The total thickness of the devices, including the substrate and encapsulation layer, is only 3 μm, which is one order of magnitude thinner than the epidermal layer of human skin. By integrating green and red PLEDs with OPDs, we fabricate an ultraflexible reflective pulse oximeter. The device unobtrusively measures the oxygen concentration of blood when laminated on a finger. On-skin seven-segment digital displays and color indicators can visualize data directly on the body.

candidates.title: Single-cell gene expression reveals a landscape of regulatory T cell phenotypes shaped by the TCR.
candidates.snippet: CD4 +  T regulatory cells (T reg ) are central to immune homeostasis, their phenotypic heterogeneity reflecting the diverse environments and target cells that they regulate. To understand this heterogeneity, we combined single-cell RNA-seq, activation reporter and T cell receptor (TCR) analysis to profile thousands of T reg  or conventional CD4 + FoxP3 -  T cells (T conv ) from mouse lymphoid organs and human blood. T reg  and T conv  pools showed areas of overlap, as resting 'furtive' T regs  with overall similarity to T convs  or as a convergence of activated states. All T regs  expressed a small core of FoxP3-dependent transcripts, onto which additional programs were added less uniformly. Among suppressive functions, Il2ra and Ctla4 were quasiconstant, inhibitory cytokines being more sparsely distributed. TCR signal intensity did not affect resting/activated T reg  proportions but molded activated T reg  programs. The main lines of T reg  heterogeneity in mice were strikingly conserved in human blood. These results reveal unexpected TCR-shaped states of activation, providing a framework to synthesize previous observations of T reg  heterogeneity.

candidates.title: In vivo quantification of spatially varying mechanical properties in developing tissues.
candidates.snippet: The mechanical properties of the cellular microenvironment and their spatiotemporal variations are thought to play a central role in sculpting embryonic tissues, maintaining organ architecture and controlling cell behavior, including cell differentiation. However, no direct in vivo and in situ measurement of mechanical properties within developing 3D tissues and organs has yet been performed. Here we introduce a technique that employs biocompatible, magnetically responsive ferrofluid microdroplets as local mechanical actuators and allows quantitative spatiotemporal measurements of mechanical properties in vivo. Using this technique, we show that vertebrate body elongation entails spatially varying tissue mechanics along the anteroposterior axis. Specifically, we find that the zebrafish tailbud is viscoelastic (elastic below a few seconds and fluid after just 1 min) and displays decreasing stiffness and increasing fluidity toward its posterior elongating region. This method opens new avenues to study mechanobiology in vivo, both in embryogenesis and in disease processes, including cancer.

candidates.snippet: The origin of charge transfer bands that develop on reaction of Old Yellow Enzyme with alpha,beta-unsaturated cyclic ketones such as 3-oxodecalin-4-ene (ODE, numbered according to the convention for steroids), 3-oxodecalin-4-ene-10-carboxaldehyde (ODEC), and 2-cyclohexenone is shown to be due to the aromatization of ODE and ODEC to 3-hydroxy-6,7,8,9-tetrahydronaphthalene (HTN) and of 2-cyclohexenone to phenol. The aromatization of ODEC to HTN is stereospecific and involves the trans dehydrogenation of the 1 beta, 2 alpha hydrogens. The aromatization occurs under aerobic as well as anaerobic conditions. With the exception of ODEC under aerobic conditions, the aromatization of these substrates is accompanied by a dismutation reaction in which the olefinic bond of a second molecule of each substrate is reduced to give the saturated cyclic ketone. Molecular oxygen may serve as the electron acceptor with ODEC and some other substrates under aerobic reaction conditions. candidates.title: Characterization of a gene product (Sec53p) required for protein assembly in the yeast endoplasmic reticulum.
candidates.snippet: SEC53, a gene that is required for completion of assembly of proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum in yeast, has been cloned, sequenced, and the product localized by cell fractionation. Complementation of a sec53 mutation is achieved with unique plasmids from genomic or cDNA expression banks. These inserts contain the authentic gene, a cloned copy of which integrates at the sec53 locus. An open reading frame in the insert predicts a 29-kD protein with no significant hydrophobic character. This prediction is confirmed by detection of a 28-kD protein overproduced in cells that carry SEC53 on a multicopy plasmid. To follow Sec53p more directly, a LacZ-SEC53 gene fusion has been constructed which allows the isolation of a hybrid protein for use in production of antibody. With such an antibody, quantitative immune decoration has shown that the sec53-6 mutation decreases the level of Sec53p at 37 degrees C, while levels comparable to wild-type are seen at 24 degrees C. An eightfold overproduction of Sec53p accompanies transformation of cells with a multicopy plasmid containing SEC53. Cell fractionation, performed with conditions that preserve the lumenal content of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), shows Sec53p highly enriched in the cytosol fraction. We suggest that Sec53p acts indirectly to facilitate assembly in the ER, possibly by interacting with a stable ER component, or by providing a small molecule, other than an oligosaccharide precursor, necessary for the assembly event.

candidates.title: Glycosylation of the core of the HIV-1 envelope subunit protein gp120 is not required for native trimer formation or viral infectivity.
candidates.snippet: The gp120 subunit of the HIV-1 envelope (Env) protein is heavily glycosylated at ∼25 glycosylation sites, of which ∼7-8 are located in the V1/V2 and V3 variable loops and the others in the remaining core gp120 region. Glycans partially shield Env from recognition by the host immune system and also are believed to be indispensable for proper folding of gp120 and for viral infectivity. Previous attempts to alter glycosylation sites in Env typically involved mutating the glycosylated asparagine residues to structurally similar glutamines or alanines. Here, we confirmed that such mutations at multiple glycosylation sites greatly diminish viral infectivity and result in significantly reduced binding to both neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. Therefore, using an alternative approach, we combined evolutionary information with structure-guided design and yeast surface display to produce properly cleaved HIV-1 Env variants that lack all 15 core gp120 glycans, yet retain conformational integrity and multiple-cycle viral infectivity and bind to several broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs), including trimer-specific antibodies and a germline-reverted version of the bNAb VRC01. Our observations demonstrate that core gp120 glycans are not essential for folding, and hence their likely primary role is enabling immune evasion. We also show that our glycan removal approach is not strain restricted. Glycan-deficient Env derivatives can be used as priming immunogens because they should engage and activate a more divergent set of germlines than fully glycosylated Env. In conclusio

candidates.title: Design of a non-glycosylated outer domain-derived HIV-1 gp120 immunogen that binds to CD4 and induces neutralizing antibodies.
candidates.snippet: The outer domain (OD) of the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein gp120 is an important target for vaccine design as it contains a number of conserved epitopes, including a large fraction of the CD4 binding site. Attempts to design OD-based immunogens in the past have met with little success. We report the design and characterization of an Escherichia coli-expressed OD-based immunogen (OD(EC)), based on the sequence of the HxBc2 strain. The OD(EC)-designed immunogen lacks the variable loops V1V2 and V3 and incorporates 11 designed mutations at the interface of the inner and the outer domains of gp120. Biophysical studies showed that OD(EC) is folded and protease-resistant, whereas OD(EC) lacking the designed mutations is highly aggregation-prone. In contrast to previously characterized OD constructs, OD(EC) bound CD4 and the broadly neutralizing antibody b12 but not the non-neutralizing antibodies b6 and F105. Upon immunization in rabbits, OD(EC) was highly immunogenic, and the sera showed measurable neutralization for four subtype B and one subtype C virus including two b12-resistant viruses. In contrast, sera from rabbits immunized with gp120 did not neutralize any of the viruses. OD(EC) is the first example of a gp120 fragment-based immunogen that yields significant neutralizing antibodies.

candidates.title: Full-length human immunodeficiency virus type 1 genomes from subtype C-infected seroconverters in India, with evidence of intersubtype recombination.
candidates.snippet: The development of an effective human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) vaccine is likely to depend on knowledge of circulating variants of genes other than the commonly sequenced gag and env genes. In addition, full-genome data are particularly limited for HIV-1 subtype C, currently the most commonly transmitted subtype in India and worldwide. Likewise, little is known about sequence variation of HIV-1 in India, the country facing the largest burden of HIV worldwide. Therefore, the objective of this study was to clone and characterize the complete genome of HIV-1 from seroconverters infected with subtype C variants in India. Cocultured HIV-1 isolates were obtained from six seroincident individuals from Pune, India, and virtually full-length HIV-1 genomes were amplified, cloned, and sequenced from each. Sequence analysis revealed that five of the six genomes were of subtype C, while one was a mosaic of subtypes A and C, with multiple breakpoints in env, nef, and the 3' long terminal repeat as determined by both maximal chi2 analysis and phylogenetic bootstrapping. Sequences were compared for preservation of known cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes. Compared with those of the HIV-1LAI sequence, 38% of well-defined CTL epitopes were identical. The proportion of nonconservative substitutions for Env, at 61%, was higher (P < 0.001) than those for Gag (24%), Pol (18%), and Nef (32%). candidates.title: RDP3: a flexible and fast computer program for analyzing recombination.
candidates.snippet: Unlabelled RDP3 is a new version of the RDP program for characterizing recombination events in DNA-sequence alignments. Among other novelties, this version includes four new recombination analysis methods (3SEQ, VISRD, PHYLRO and LDHAT), new tests for recombination hot-spots, a range of matrix methods for visualizing over-all patterns of recombination within datasets and recombination-aware ancestral sequence reconstruction. Complementary to a high degree of analysis flow automation, RDP3 also has a highly interactive and detailed graphical user interface that enables more focused hands-on cross-checking of results with a wide variety of newly implemented phylogenetic tree construction and matrix-based recombination signal visualization methods. The new RDP3 can accommodate large datasets and is capable of analyzing alignments ranging in size from 1000 × 10 kilobase sequences to 20 × 2 megabase sequences within 48 h on a desktop PC. Availability RDP3 is available for free from its web site http://darwin.uvigo.es/rdp/rdp.html.

candidates.title: Structure, function, and evolution of bacterial ATP-binding cassette systems.
candidates.snippet: Summary ATP-binding cassette (ABC) systems are universally distributed among living organisms and function in many different aspects of bacterial physiology. ABC transporters are best known for their role in the import of essential nutrients and the export of toxic molecules, but they can also mediate the transport of many other physiological substrates. In a classical transport reaction, two highly conserved ATP-binding domains or subunits couple the binding/hydrolysis of ATP to the translocation of particular substrates across the membrane, through interactions with membrane-spanning domains of the transporter. Variations on this basic theme involve soluble ABC ATP-binding proteins that couple ATP hydrolysis to nontransport processes, such as DNA repair and gene expression regulation. Insights into the structure, function, and mechanism of action of bacterial ABC proteins are reported, based on phylogenetic comparisons as well as classic biochemical and genetic approaches. The availability of an increasing number of high-resolution structures has provided a valuable framework for interpretation of recent studies, and realistic models have been proposed to explain how these fascinating molecular machines use complex dynamic processes to fulfill their numerous biological functions. These advances are also important for elucidating the mechanism of action of eukaryotic ABC proteins, because functional defects in many of them are responsible for severe human inherited diseases.

candidates.title: Full-genome evolutionary analysis of the novel corona virus (2019-nCoV) rejects the hypothesis of emergence as a result of a recent recombination event.
candidates.snippet: Background A novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV) associated with human to human transmission and severe human infection has been recently reported from the city of Wuhan in China. Our objectives were to characterize the genetic relationships of the 2019-nCoV and to search for putative recombination within the subgenus of sarbecovirus. Methods Putative recombination was investigated by RDP4 and Simplot v3.5.1 and discordant phylogenetic clustering in individual genomic fragments was confirmed by phylogenetic analysis using maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods. Results Our analysis suggests that the 2019-nCoV although closely related to BatCoV RaTG13 sequence throughout the genome (sequence similarity 96.3%), shows discordant clustering with the Bat_SARS-like coronavirus sequences. Specifically, in the 5'-part spanning the first 11,498 nucleotides and the last 3'-part spanning 24,341-30,696 positions, 2019-nCoV and RaTG13 formed a single cluster with Bat_SARS-like coronavirus sequences, whereas in the middle region spanning the 3'-end of ORF1a, the ORF1b and almost half of the spike regions, 2019-nCoV and RaTG13 grouped in a separate distant lineage within the sarbecovirus branch. Conclusions The levels of genetic similarity between the 2019-nCoV and RaTG13 suggest that the latter does not provide the exact variant that caused the outbreak in humans, but the hypothesis that 2019-nCoV has originated from bats is very likely. candidates.title: S1 gene-based phylogeny of infectious bronchitis virus: An attempt to harmonize virus classification.
candidates.snippet: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) is the causative agent of a highly contagious disease that results in severe economic losses to the global poultry industry. The virus exists in a wide variety of genetically distinct viral types, and both phylogenetic analysis and measures of pairwise similarity among nucleotide or amino acid sequences have been used to classify IBV strains. However, there is currently no consensus on the method by which IBV sequences should be compared, and heterogeneous genetic group designations that are inconsistent with phylogenetic history have been adopted, leading to the confusing coexistence of multiple genotyping schemes. Herein, we propose a simple and repeatable phylogeny-based classification system combined with an unambiguous and rationale lineage nomenclature for the assignment of IBV strains. By using complete nucleotide sequences of the S1 gene we determined the phylogenetic structure of IBV, which in turn allowed us to define 6 genotypes that together comprise 32 distinct viral lineages and a number of inter-lineage recombinants. Because of extensive rate variation among IBVs, we suggest that the inference of phylogenetic relationships alone represents a more appropriate criterion for sequence classification than pairwise sequence comparisons. The adoption of an internationally accepted viral nomenclature is crucial for future studies of IBV epidemiology and evolution, and the classification scheme presented here can be updated and revised novel S1 sequences should become available.

candidates.title: Theoretical analysis of Lumry-Eyring models in differential scanning calorimetry.
candidates.snippet: A theoretical analysis of several protein denaturation models (Lumry-Eyring models) that include a rate-limited step leading to an irreversibly denatured state of the protein (the final state) has been carried out. The differential scanning calorimetry transitions predicted for these models can be broadly classified into four groups: situations A, B, C, and C'. (A) The transition is calorimetrically irreversible but the rate-limited, irreversible step takes place with significant rate only at temperatures slightly above those corresponding to the transition. Equilibrium thermodynamics analysis is permissible. (B) The transition is distorted by the occurrence of the rate-limited step; nevertheless, it contains thermodynamic information about the reversible unfolding of the protein, which could be obtained upon the appropriate data treatment. (C) The heat absorption is entirely determined by the kinetics of formation of the final state and no thermodynamic information can be extracted from the calorimetric transition; the rate-determining step is the irreversible process itself. (C') same as C, but, in this case, the rate-determining step is a previous step in the unfolding pathway. It is shown that ligand and protein concentration effects on transitions corresponding to situation C (strongly rate-limited transitions) are similar to those predicted by equilibrium thermodynamics for simple reversible unfolding models. candidates.title: A selective chemical probe for exploring the role of CDK8 and CDK19 in human disease.
candidates.snippet: There is unmet need for chemical tools to explore the role of the Mediator complex in human pathologies ranging from cancer to cardiovascular disease. Here we determine that CCT251545, a small-molecule inhibitor of the WNT pathway discovered through cell-based screening, is a potent and selective chemical probe for the human Mediator complex-associated protein kinases CDK8 and CDK19 with >100-fold selectivity over 291 other kinases. X-ray crystallography demonstrates a type 1 binding mode involving insertion of the CDK8 C terminus into the ligand binding site. In contrast to type II inhibitors of CDK8 and CDK19, CCT251545 displays potent cell-based activity. We show that CCT251545 and close analogs alter WNT pathway-regulated gene expression and other on-target effects of modulating CDK8 and CDK19, including expression of genes regulated by STAT1. Consistent with this, we find that phosphorylation of STAT1(SER727) is a biomarker of CDK8 kinase activity in vitro and in vivo. Finally, we demonstrate in vivo activity of CCT251545 in WNT-dependent tumors.

candidates.title: Analysis of the Escherichia coli genome. III. DNA sequence of the region from 87.2 to 89.2 minutes.
candidates.snippet: The DNA sequence of 96.5 kilobases of the Escherichia coli K-12 genome has been determined, spanning the region between rrnA at 87.2 minutes and katG at 89.2 minutes on the genetic map. The sequence includes 84 open reading frames, of which 46 code for unidentified proteins. Six previously mapped but unsequenced genes have been identified in this span: mob, fdhD, rhaD, rhaA, rhaB, and kdgT. In addition, five new genes have been assigned: the heat shock genes hsIU and hsIV, and the genes fdoG, fdoH, and fdoI, which encode the three subunits of formate dehydrogenase-O. The arrangement of the genes relative to possible promoters and terminators suggests 57 potential transcription units. Other features include the precise location of the bacteriophage P2 attachment site attP2II, and eleven REP elements, including one containing 9 REP sequences--one of the largest such elements known. This segment brings the total length of contiguous finished sequence to 325 kilobases.

candidates.title: Addressing the psychological impact of COVID-19 on healthcare workers: learning from a systematic review of early interventions for frontline responders.
candidates.snippet: Objectives Protecting healthcare workers from psychological harm is an urgent clinical issue within the current COVID-19 pandemic. Research on early psychological programmes that aim to prevent or reduce mental health symptoms and that have been tested in frontline responders may assist service providers with choosing a suitable intervention for rapid dissemination in healthcare settings. Design and outcome measures First, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO and Google Scholar were searched through a systematic literature review of early psychological interventions administered to frontline responders in the last 15 years. Interventions were included if they were designed to prevent or reduce psychological impact and had outcome measures of psychological distress (eg, general psychopathology, post-traumatic stress disorder and stress) and/or positive mental health domains (eg, resilience, self-efficacy and life satisfaction). Second, the suitability of these programmes for the healthcare workforce was evaluated according to the criteria of effectiveness, content applicability and feasibility. Results Of 320 articles retrieved, 12 relevant studies were included that described six early psychological interventions. Although the evidence base is limited, psychological first aid, eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing, and trauma risk management showed effectiveness across at least two studies each with frontline workers. candidates.title: Radioresistance of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers and Therapeutic Perspectives.
candidates.snippet: Survival in unresectable locally advanced stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients remains poor despite chemoradiotherapy. Recently, adjuvant immunotherapy improved survival for these patients but we are still far from curing most of the patients with only a 57% survival remaining at 3 years. This poor survival is due to the resistance to chemoradiotherapy, local relapses, and distant relapses. Several biological mechanisms have been found to be involved in the chemoradioresistance such as cancer stem cells, cancer mutation status, or the immune system. New drugs to overcome this radioresistance in NSCLCs have been investigated such as radiosensitizer treatments or immunotherapies. Different modalities of radiotherapy have also been investigated to improve efficacity such as dose escalation or proton irradiations. In this review, we focused on biological mechanisms such as the cancer stem cells, the cancer mutations, the antitumor immune response in the first part, then we explored some strategies to overcome this radioresistance in stage III NSCLCs with new drugs or radiotherapy modalities.
